Sourdough bread rises through wild yeast fermentation. The starter must be fed
with flour and water daily to keep the culture active and the dough vigorous.

Gluten develops as dough is kneaded, forming an elastic network that traps the
carbon dioxide produced during fermentation and gives bread its airy crumb.

Oven temperature matters enormously: a hot stone and steam in the first minutes
of baking produce a crisp crust and good oven spring in the finished loaf.
